Resident Evil's change of perspective matters

A quite interesting article. While I do agree that the first person perspective allows for a deeper immersion (doubly so now that VR technology is beginning to build up), I also would argue that the emotional impact a third-person perspective can have on the player can be equally potent when it comes to making horror games scary:

Rather than having nasty things happen to a first-person character (i.e., an avatar of the player himself), having the same nasty things happen to a third-person character (i.e. a totally distinct character whose survival lies in the player's hands) imho produces a much stronger feeling of horror - and, more importantly, guilt. Seeing your own avatar die is one thing, but considering yourself responsible for the death of a third-person character is quite another.

To this effect, I would also argue that things like tank controls and fixed cameras as found in the early 3d horror games greatly contribute to this - by preventing the player from identifying as the player character via these fairly arbitrary barriers, you create the position of an outside observer on whose help and guidance the player character is dependent. Coupled with our inherent fear about loss of control, the chance of being responsible for the death of someone else really makes your skin crawl, especially if the playable character is female and/or young, that is, a type of character which already invokes the protector instinct of the (predominantly) player.

It feels weird to see Resi being super serious now when it's the same series that had "Jill Sandwich", "Master of Unlocking", "The president's daughter has got ballistics", and Motorcycling over skyscrapers/boulder punching.
I completely agree with the first person school of thought. I won't even play an RPG without it.
